issues.legal_issue: A widow’s share in a deceased coparcener’s property includes both the share she would receive in a partition immediately before his death and her share by succession in his interest in the coparcenary property.
material_facts: The properties were found to belong to a joint family, and no prior partition had taken place.
The deceased had an interest in Mitakshara coparcenary property and died leaving a widow, sons, and daughters, including female heirs in Class I.
The deceased had made no testamentary disposition.
At the notional partition immediately before his death, the widow would have received a share equal to that of a son.
The Court calculated the widow’s share as the share received at the notional partition together with her equal share in the deceased’s interest by intestate succession.
issues.conclusion: The widow was entitled to both her share at the notional partition and her share by succession in the deceased’s coparcenary interest; her total share was 7/24.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 6 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, the proviso makes the deceased coparcener’s interest devolve by testamentary or intestate succession, rather than survivorship, when the specified female relative or qualifying male relative survives him. Explanation 1 requires the deceased’s interest to be calculated as the share he would have received in a partition immediately before death. The partition fiction must be given full effect throughout the calculation of the heirs’ shares: its consequences cannot be used to determine the deceased’s share and then disregarded when determining the heirs’ shares. The heir therefore receives the share obtained, or deemed to have been obtained, in the notional partition as well as the heir’s share in the deceased’s interest. Sections 8, 9, and 10 govern the relevant intestate succession calculation. The Court applied Commissioner of Income Tax, Delhi v. S. Teja Singh and approved the reasoning in East End Dwellings Co. Ltd. v. Finsbury Borough Council on giving full effect to a statutory fiction. It also approved Rangubai Lalji v. Laxman Lalji, Sushilabai Ramachandra Kulkarni v. Narayanrao Gopalrao Deshpande, Vidyaben v. Jagadishchandra N. Bhatt, and Ananda v. Haribandhu.

rule.if: claim_for_heir_share_in_coparcenary_property and deceased_coparcener_had_property_interest and class_i_female_heir_survived and no_testamentary_disposition and widow_entitled_to_share_at_partition

predicates.claim_for_heir_share_in_coparcenary_prop: An heir claimed a share in property in which the deceased had held a coparcenary interest.
predicates.deceased_coparcener_had_property_interes: The deceased held an interest in the coparcenary property when he died.
predicates.class_i_female_heir_survived: A female heir in the relevant class survived the deceased.
predicates.no_testamentary_disposition: The deceased left no testamentary disposition governing the devolution of his interest.
predicates.widow_entitled_to_share_at_partition: The widow would have received a share if a partition had taken place immediately before the deceased’s death.

issues.definition: When the stated conditions apply, the widow receives both the share attributed to her at the partition and her inheritance share in the deceased’s interest.
